items.author: main session (Ben, 2026-11-05: playtest list and design form)
items.title: A mine costs six months of net at the opening; ease over 10-20 years through reinvestment
items.design: Playtest item 20, Ben's most important. Ruling (Ben, 2026-11-05) in the authority doc. Target: a mine costs about 6 months of a major's net at the opening, back to about 1 month after 10-20 years; 6x in 15 years is about 13% a year, or roughly an 8-year payback on a good building. Cost lives mostly in materials, so a planned steel chain is the edge. Good sites pay back in years, poor ones barely: the finder stays open (Ben declined gating it), so this spread is the WHOLE reward for searching and must be read, not assumed. Calibrate from the payback census; multipliers are in-band. RISKS: raises steel demand and can stretch or pause sites (max_stretch); rivals barely build today (median 44 to about 47 in five years), so read whether they stall further; read against BL-1494 (tick-50 stall). Check: market-viability, opening-parity, rebless-shape-probe. One re-bless shared with the other world-movers. CALIBRATION from the census (BL-1496): six months of net at the measured 1,000-1,150 a quarter is a mine of about 2,000-2,300, about 5-6x today's 327-430. Reinvestment grows income at 1/payback whatever the net: a x5.5 mine pays back in about 5 years on produce (0.9 today), 9 on copper, 21 on iron, 40 on coal; standing processors in about 15-25 years. Background growth of about 4.7% a year carries about 2.5x of the 6x over 20 years, leaving about 2.4x for reinvestment, so x5-6 looks feasible and must be run, not assumed. Timber, fibre and stone mines cost about 105-110 today with no steel in the bill: the materials lever must reach them. Read net after research: see the review queue.

items.design: Ben, 2026-11-07: every major's kit gains a Planetary Marketplace on the market of its steel slot, the same for all. No major traded from its own mill market once; 39% of stranded steel had no trade building at the source. Merged 2026-11-08 with the opening lane.

items.design: Ben, 2026-11-07: the code wins. A shipment draws Logistic Points at the market it leaves, not along its whole route; LOGISTICS.md's whole-route sentence (NR-1060) is rewritten to match. Merged 2026-11-08 with the opening lane.

items.author: main session (Ben, 2026-11-07: steel trade form)
items.title: Logistic Points drawn by cargo value
items.design: Ben, 2026-11-07, this sprint: a shipment draws Logistic Points by its cargo's value, not its unit count. Per unit, coal costs about 8 times steel per credit; the cap refused 39-55% of shipments. Kept after measuring (Ben, 2026-11-08). Constant 3.98: base value per point that holds the summed q20 draw of rulings 1-3 (3,909 units). Merged.

items.title: Site finder building grid with province scope
items.design: Built and merged at 0fdd6a23; the design is in construction.md. Stays open for Ben's live click: a cell press arms the lens and a second clears it; a province tile narrows the grid and a table row press does not; Clear returns the whole body and deselects; the roughly 5 s pending fill is acceptable; wheel-scroll inside the grid; hover cards on figure, count and dimmed cells. Open for Ben: a selected tile scopes the grid, so the home surface opens scoped. Requested verify reads, none granted: picker_rows net_text and sites, the Clear press position, a pending-cell count.

items.title: A declaration makes both sides hostile; a last province ends the nation
items.design: Ben, 2026-11-09 form. Design in RELATIONS.md section 7 and NATIONS.md section Elimination. declare_war writes both hostility rows; check_peace_terms admits the last province; elimination closes the loser's wars, clears its rows, disbands its units, passes a positive treasury to the conqueror, flags it ended. The player's nation ending is a lost campaign, then spectate. Fixes Ben's stuck war ("Not hostile" on a front after a declaration on him).
